scope: Engineering review of the exact source, package versions, architectures, and default Compose recipe. These records do not accept risk for a partner, certify an installed environment, remove raw findings, or permit unsupported software. Reassess custom or retained configuration and deployment conditions. Each disposition records its required deployment predicates, review date, and expiry.

The exact images remove set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits, retain an empty fstab, and run with no-new-privileges, restricted capabilities, read-only roots, and no host data mounts. These controls remove the default privileged user-mount path and limit host impact; they do not repair the library or protect writable container data after process compromise. Privileged containers, user fstab entries, or custom mount/ACL operations require reassessment.

Image Git configuration evidence does not inspect a partner volume. A compromised allowed forge or service remains a residual risk.

Native XML parsing remains installed. Sediment exposes neither arbitrary SQL nor XML operations and uses bound SQL parameters. Database network and credential isolation reduce access; resource limits and process confinement reduce host impact. The exact Wolfi zlib 1.3.2-r7 library remains installed and implements the affected non-blocking gzip-file write API; this record does not claim a backported fix. Exact-image ELF inspection finds no dynamic importer of that API and no static embed outside the reviewed lxml.etree, lxml.objectify, and xmlsec extensions. Manual review of the pinned LiteLLM SAML handler and python3-saml callers finds that untrusted XML is parsed from memory, XML output is serialized to memory, and XMLSec keys and certificates are loaded from memory. Schema validation also parses trusted packaged XSD files through already-open file objects; it does not open a non-blocking gzFile writer. The reviewed caller sources match the final AMD64 and ARM64 images byte for byte. These absent call prerequisites support not_affected for the exact reviewed images, not a claim that zlib is fixed. The symbol predicate detects changed native imports and static-embed paths; it does not inspect Python callers. A changed caller, gzip-file output path, native importer, static embed, dependency, or deployment extension requires reassessment.

The exact Debian bookworm libexpat1 2.5.0-1+deb12u3 package remains vulnerable to quadratic CPU consumption while parsing XML attributes. Debian postpones the bookworm fix. Sediment's authenticated ingest routes parse JSON, and its service mirror paths invoke Git clone/fetch rather than HTTP push or XML parsing. The installed Git HTTP-push helper and Expat library remain present; complete helper reachability is not proven. Source-reviewed clone-host restrictions, two mirror workers, a queue of sixteen, a 120-second process-group execution budget, and the supplied container resource limits reduce exposure and bound one operation. These controls do not fix Expat or prevent repeated eligible work from denying service. A compromised allowed forge, custom Git helpers or configuration, operator/client push usage, or an added XML-consuming service path requires reassessment. This is mitigation with residual availability risk, not non-applicability.

The exact Debian source retains the unchecked qualified-name dictionary arithmetic and native parsing remains installed. Sediment exposes neither arbitrary SQL nor XML operations. Database access restrictions reduce access to native parsing; confinement reduces host impact. Parser name limits constrain the reviewed PostgreSQL document path, but complete caller bounds and exploitability were not verified. An ordinary SQL role can invoke native XML. These controls do not repair the library or protect the Fact volume and database availability after native process compromise.

The exact Debian source xmlURIEscapeStr rejects a nonpositive xmlStrlen result, equivalent to the cited upstream correction for length saturation. The guard also exists in the original 2.9.14 source, while Debian still marks this package vulnerable. Retain a conservative mitigated classification pending resolution of that discrepancy. Database access restrictions and process confinement reduce exposure; this source comparison does not establish a vendor fix, prove absence of other URI arithmetic defects, or verify every binary caller. Native XML remains accessible to an ordinary SQL role, and native process compromise can affect the Fact volume and database availability.

The exact Debian source retains the affected XPointer allocation. The reviewed PostgreSQL XML implementation invokes XPath compilation and evaluation, not XPointer; those are distinct APIs. Sediment exposes no XPointer interface. Database access restrictions and process confinement reduce exposure. Libxml2 XInclude can call XPointer, so optional extensions and other native callers require reassessment. Whole-image non-reachability and exploitation were not verified. The controls do not repair the installed library or protect the Fact volume and database availability after native process compromise.

The exact Debian source retains unchecked output callback length narrowing. PostgreSQL XML serialization reaches a buffer callback through xmlSaveToBuffer; that path is not absent. Sediment exposes neither XML serialization nor arbitrary SQL. Database access restrictions reduce access; resource limits and confinement reduce host impact. The callback overflow threshold was not reproduced or proven unreachable, and PostgreSQL datum limits are not a general bound on libxml allocations. An ordinary SQL role can invoke native XML. Native process compromise can affect the Fact volume, and exhaustion can stop the database.

The exact Debian source retains XInclude entry points that reset parser flags. The reviewed PostgreSQL XML implementation does not call XInclude processing and installs an external-entity loader that returns empty input. This is evidence about that path, not every native consumer. Database network isolation and credential separation further reduce exposure. Added XML extensions, native callers, or loader changes require reassessment. Network isolation does not prevent local file reads, and read-only roots do not provide confidentiality or protect the Fact volume after process compromise.
